subject: Animation
title: Persistence of Vision: How Animation Tricks the Eye
description: One-minute skill: Persistence of Vision: How Animation Tricks the Eye.

hook.text: Animation works because your brain blends rapidly shown still images into the illusion of smooth motion.

buildup.text: At 24 frames per second, each image stays on screen for just 42 milliseconds before the next appears.

discovery.text: Your retina retains each image briefly, and your brain fills the gap between frames to create flow.

twist.text: Scientists now debate whether persistence of vision fully explains the effect. The brain's role may be more complex.

climax.text: The entire animation industry exists because of a quirk in human visual perception discovered centuries ago.

punchline.text: Your brain's inability to see gaps made animation possible.

quiz.question: How does persistence of vision enable animation?
options: The projector adds extra frames between drawings
The brain retains each image briefly and fills gaps between frames, creating the illusion of smooth motion
Animation uses special screens that blend images together
